topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets expectations for students from different academic backgrounds.

topics.label: Biological foundations and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the genetic and epigenetic alterations underlying cancer development, the disruption of normal tissue architecture, and the cell culture models used to study these properties.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and tumour progression
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how tumours progress from benign to invasive and metastatic states using clinical, histological, and tissue-level examples.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: It defines the conventional naming rules and clinical exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumours based on their tissue origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological and anatomical mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumours cause illness and patient death.

topics.label: Patterns of tumour incidence across species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare the frequency and types of benign and malignant tumours across human populations and other animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical practice of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the rationale, histological basis, and diagnostic challenges of population screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Conclusion and practical session reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and practical session logistics.
